title: Felix and the Songbook
premise: Mara Okafor has spent eleven years keeping her grandmother's lighthouse and an old songbook of letters she never sent to Felix Adeyemi, the composer who left their coastal town for a career in Lagos. When a storm washes up a lost letter — postmarked the week he left, never delivered — Mara discovers Felix is returning to premiere a symphony built from her unsent words, believing them written by her late grandmother. To claim her own voice, Mara must confess the authorship before the concert ends, risking his anger and her carefully guarded heart. He chooses her over the myth, and together they rewrite the final movement as a duet.
about_author: Tamsin Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who grew up between a fishing village and a city library, and writes love stories about people who arrive too late but stay anyway. She lives by the sea with a dog named Postscript.

chapters.title: The Tide Brings Back What It Takes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. After a winter storm, Mara finds a water-stained letter in the rocks below the lighthouse — one of her own unsent letters to Felix, postmarked eleven years ago, returned undelivered. The discovery cracks open the life she's built around silence. Emotional beat: dread mixed with longing, as the past refuses to stay buried.

chapters.title: A Symphony in Someone Else's Name
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Felix returns to town to premiere 'The Keeper's Song,' a symphony he believes his mentor — Mara's grandmother — composed from her letters. Mara attends the rehearsal and hears her private words orchestrated for a full hall. Emotional beat: vertigo and quiet fury; her most intimate self has become public property under a false name.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Saw
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing on Felix's. On the night of the premiere, Mara confronts Felix backstage, but duty intervenes: the symphony's patron threatens to withdraw funding if the 'authorship scandal' surfaces, and Felix must choose between the career that took him away and the truth. Emotional beat: climax — Mara says the rehearsed sentence mid-performance, claiming the songbook aloud as the hall goes silent.

chapters.title: Second Movement
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the aftermath, Felix publicly credits Mara, walks away from the patron, and asks for eleven years back — not as apology, but as invitation. They compose a new piece together at the lighthouse, her words and his music finally signed by the same hand. Emotional beat: resolution; second chances belong to those brave enough to keep time.
